subject: wizardBookshelf
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: wizard's bookshelf with tomes, scrolls, orbs and candles.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm designing a static bookshelf model—roughly 2.2m tall, dark wood with gilt trim, a carved arched top featuring a crescent moon and stars, four shelves holding varied colorful tomes with decorative spine details.

I'm sketching out helper functions to build boxes and books, planning each book as a thin cover shell wrapping a slightly inset page block, with the spine facing forward.

For the spine decoration, I'm considering using a greyscale texture that gets tinted by the color prop, so I can paint gilt bands and a title plate without spending extra draw calls per book color variant.

Now I'm sketching the overall bookshelf frame: outer dimensions, side panel thickness, plinth height, and the y-positions for each shelf board, with a top board to carry the crown molding.

I'm planning compartment contents per shelf: bottom shelf with stacked tomes and a standing row, next shelves adding scroll racks, an orb on a stand, candles, hourglass, and leaning books, topped by a crescent ornament and crown arch above the top board.

For the top I'm placing a large glowing orb on a gilt stand flanked by candle clusters, with an arched pediment behind bearing star emblems. For candles I'm building wax cylinders with gilt dishes and layered glowing flames (orange outer, yellow inner), sometimes resting atop book stacks, and the orb itself as a glowing sphere with an inner swirl of color.

Now I'm texturing the orb with a radial gradient and sparkles for a magical glow effect, adding a gilt stand with prongs beneath it, then designing parchment scrolls with darker end rolls, wooden knobs, and red ribbon bands arranged in a pyramid stack on a shelf.

I'm also adding a few upright scrolls in a jar and a hanging unfurled scroll using a textured plane with runes, attaching it to the front edge of a shelf so it curls down slightly without blocking the books below.

For the other details, I'm building an hourglass from two lathed cones of sand-colored glass with gilt caps and posts, a lathed potion flask with glowing green liquid and a cork, a glowing purple crystal cluster from flattened octahedron geometry, and a small owl figurine made of spheres for the body and head, a cone beak, ear tufts, and wings, perched on the top shelf corner for character. I'm skipping the skull and wizard hat ideas, and now setting up the wood grain coloring with dark and light tones for countershading.

I'm applying grain texture along different axes for the side panels and shelves, importing gilt and brass metal materials from the clockwork kit, and planning carved pilasters with gilt strips on the sides plus a carved rune frieze board beneath the crown using a textured rune band over dark wood.

For the crown itself, I'm building a pediment shape extruded in dark wood with a gilt crescent moon and five-point stars cut and placed at center front, computing the crescent and star outlines programmatically and orienting the extrusion so it faces forward correctly.

Now I'm working out the pointed gothic arch outline for the pediment, computing a symmetric curve from the base corners up to a sharp apex using interpolated points rather than a simple polygon.

I want to add gilt spike finials at the top and smaller gilt spheres/cones at the side corners. For the books, I'm thinking about simplifying the part count—body box for the cover plus a protruding pages box instead of separate spine/boards/bands—to keep the total object count manageable around 250.

For leaning books, I'm considering treating each as a compound object with its own rotation pivot rather than composing it from separate rotated pieces, to keep the geometry simple.

I need to generalize the book function for both flat and standing orientations — boards positioned differently depending on mode, and spine textures need separate treatments: horizontal bands for standing spines versus vertical lines for flat books lying down.

Confirming the band orientation checks out for the flat spine case. For the lean rotation on the standing book, I can't combine a dir vector with a rotation value directly, so I'll compute a quaternion from the z-axis angle instead and apply that as the base orientation.

For the flat geometry, I'll pre-rotate it around z by 90° so the texture orientation lines up correctly, and keep lean at 0 for most flat cases. I'll keep the gold trim color consistent across texture variants, starting with spine pattern A featuring top/bottom bands and a diamond center.

Now I'm defining three spine variants and an anime-inspired color palette of crimson, royal blue, emerald, violet, teal, burgundy, ochre, and midnight tones. I'm also working out the shelf layout math — inner x and z bounds, book depth and positioning so fronts align at a consistent z, and shelf top y-values for placement.

I realize the gap between the top shelf and top board is too narrow, so I'm adjusting the shelf spacing (surfaces around 0.16, 0.62, 1.08, 1.54) and shifting the top board position to give the top compartment enough clear height.

Now I'm planning the overall structure: 4 compartments plus a top shelf, with a crown frieze and pediment on top bringing total height to roughly 2.75m. I'm writing a helper function to lay out rows of books on each shelf, specifying thickness, height, color, and spine texture for each book, starting with the bottom compartment's mix of standing books and stacked tomes.

Each compartment gets its own curated clutter: candles, skulls, crystal clusters, potion bottles, scroll pyramids, orbs on stands, hourglasses, and brass jars with scrolls, distributed across the four shelves so no two look identical while keeping a consistent wizard-study aesthetic.

For the candles themselves, I'll parametrize them with a gilt dish base, cream wax cylinder, small drip details, a dark wick, and a layered flame glow. I'm also considering optional brass wall sconces flanking the shelf for an extra anime-style decorative touch.

Now I'm designing the orb and stand: a lathed gilt base dish supporting a sphere, with prong-like claws or a thin ring to cradle it at the equator, keeping the geometry simple but decorative.

For the orb's surface, I'm planning a generative texture function with radial gradients, sparkles, and swirl lines, producing three color variants—violet, cyan, and amber—so I'll need three separate textures. Tallying everything up: spine textures A/B/C, frieze, three orb variants, hanging parchment runes, an owl eye, and a flame gives about ten textures total. I'm also deciding to share a single gilt-painted sheet across the many small trim parts to keep things efficient, and planning a custom wood paint with grain mixed into a darker base and a lighter top layer.

Now I'm working through the cabinet's vertical measurements—placing a dark frieze board around y 2.0-2.12, adding an overhanging cornice box for the crown, and recalculating exact board thicknesses so the top surface lands consistently around y 2.005 given the shelf and side heights.

Realizing the frieze would collide with anything sitting on the top surface, I decide to skip a full pediment there and instead place a rear crest panel behind the top items—a wide arch shape with a moon and stars motif rising from the back of the top surface, keeping the front open for the decorative pieces.

Setting topC at 2.0, I work out the apron sits 1.875–1.975, giving compartment 3 a clear space of 0.335 so books there need to stay under 0.31. I apply the same clearance logic to the other compartments, each capped around 0.40, and plan a thin gilt trim strip along each shelf's front edge for detail. For the crest, I'm sketching a rear arch panel centered at the top surface with gothic styling, roughly 1.4 wide and 0.75 tall.

Now I'm layering the gilt emblem pieces, a crescent and star, slightly in front of the crest panel, nudging their z-depths so the thin extrusions stack without clipping. I'm also positioning a central orb above the surface with the moon emblem sitting above it, sizing the radii so the proportions look balanced together.

Next I'm working out the shelf's side panel geometry—setting their x-offsets and widths so they fit within the overall 1.5 unit frame, giving the panels a shallow depth with a thin back panel. I'm adding gilt vertical pilaster strips to the front faces of the side panels and starting to block out the plinth base beneath everything.

Continuing plinth and base geometry... placing a skirt panel and deciding to skip the claw feet for now to keep things simple, aligning everything so the plinth sits flush at y=0. I'm also setting up a helper for placing decorative orbs and starting to position an owl figure near the top right of the piece.

Now building the owl itself: scaling spheres for body and head, planning yellow eye textures with black pupils and highlights, a small orange beak cone, ear tufts, wing spheres, and tiny foot cones. I'm thinking cream and brown tones with a pale belly, and considering adding a cute little wizard hat on top for charm.

Now I'm designing the other props -- an hourglass, a glowing potion flask with teal glass and a green glowing liquid, gilt neck ring and cork, plus a violet-cyan crystal cluster made from scaled octahedrons with slight rotations for a natural crystal look.

Still building the scroll helper: a paper cylinder with darker ringed ends to suggest rolled edges, a visible dark core extending past the ends, tiny wooden knob spheres, and a red ribbon wrap at the midpoint -- around five parts per scroll.

I'm debating whether to add a hanging parchment banner with rune texture somewhere on the cabinet, but placements like the apron or side panel would cover other details, so I'll likely skip hanging it and instead consider a flat unrolled scroll lying on a shelf.

Actually, I'll add an open book near the top left crest area — a cover box with two angled page blocks textured with glowing runes, positioned at (-0.4, 2.025). Above it I'll float a few small glowing glyph cards with diamond patterns, oriented vertically, to give that corner some magical detail.

Now I'm setting up the import statements, pulling in the builder utilities and the clockwork and glow kits, confirming these are all re-exported from the SDK's main index. I'm starting the static prop group for the wizard bookshelf, noting that parts without bones won't need joints.

Writing helper functions...

Still defining book geometry...

Pages box sits inset within the covers, and I'm working out the decal plane's rotation so its width and height map correctly onto the book's y and x axes after a 90° z-rotation. For flat books I'll also add a small yaw rotation around y to give a casual, slightly scattered stacking look.

Now I'm figuring out how to combine the yaw and lean rotations consistently—flat books use yaw only, standing books use lean only, and I need a transform function that rotates local offsets correctly depending on Euler rotation order (X then Y then Z).

I'm writing a row-layout helper that places items side by side, computing x-centers and spacing based on item width, with extra gap added for leaning items based on their height and lean angle so they don't overlap their neighbors.

Adding candle geometry function...

Better to orient scrolls along z so their spiral ends face forward, giving each a circular textured disc at the front with a ribbon band wrapped around the cylindrical body.

For the jar, I'm thinking a lathed gilt-brass vessel with upright scrolls poking out — four small cylinders with ribbons tilted slightly, sitting atop a lathe profile that traces out from the axis and back to form a closed, non-self-intersecting silhouette.

For the hourglass, I'm planning gilt cylinder caps with a pinched glass bulb shape in between, lathed from an outline that narrows at the waist.

I'm reconsidering the glass approach—opaque glass would hide the sand, so I should make the bulbs pale translucent-colored instead, maybe light cyan, so the sand reads as a visible inner element rather than being obscured.

Now I'm sketching a potion bottle using a lathe profile for the curved glass body, giving it a glowing green tint, adding a cork cylinder, a gilt neck ring, and considering a second pink potion variant.

For the open book on the top left, I'm positioning a dark red cover box and two page blocks that tilt slightly toward the center using opposing z-rotations, so the pages appear to rise and meet like an open spread, with flat plane textures for the page surfaces.

Lowering glow strength to 0.45 so pages don't look fully saturated regardless of lighting. Adding three floating glyph planes with glowing cyan rune-circle textures near the crest, sized and positioned around (-0.38, 2.3-2.4), though I notice they might overlap with the crest stars positioned at ±0.45.

Now I'm placing wall sconces on the outer side panels at x=±0.75-0.83, with a gilt back plate, an arm rod, and a candle dish, mirrored left and right at y=1.45. Skipping the banner idea for now and moving to designing a frieze texture with repeating gold diamond motifs, circles, and small runes on a transparent background.

I'm then positioning the apron board, front trim, and shelf boards with precise z-depth and size values to get the overhangs and gilt edging to line up correctly around the front face.

For the rear panel, I'm deciding to paint it a mottled midnight blue-purple using a cellular noise function to scatter pale yellow star-like speckles, giving the back of the cabinet a starry-night texture instead of plain wood.

Now I'm working out the crescent moon geometry: I'm placing an outer circle and an offset inner circle, then computing their intersection points so the arc between them forms a clean crescent shape opening to the right.

I'm finalizing the vesica outline path, tracing the outer arc from 49.5° to 310.5° then the inner arc decreasing back to the top intersection with 12 steps each and sharp tips. For the star shape I'll use a 5-point outline with outer radius R and inner radius 0.45R rotated to point upward, and for the corner finials I'll place small gilt spheres with spikes at the side panel tops, skipping the crest finial.

Now I'm setting up color constants for gilt and brass metal, then building the owl figure piece by piece — body, cream belly, head, tilted ear cones, and simple eye circles, positioned relative to a base point.

Still placing owl details...

Brim sits comfortably within the head radius so it won't clip the eyes. I'm picking owl colors (brownish "#8b6b4f" and cream "#f3e3c3"), then writing a texture-generating function for the orb that creates an SVG with a vertical gradient, swirling paths, and sparkle dots to simulate a magical glowing surface when mapped onto the sphere.

Now I'm designing the eye texture for the owl using a gold circle with a pupil, plus a spiral texture for the scroll ends with a parchment-colored disc and a hand-computed spiral stroke path bordered by a circle. For the rune text, I'm setting up a seeded random number generator so I can deterministically produce small glyph-like strokes to scatter across surfaces, which I'll reuse for the parchment page texture with ink-colored rune lines.

I'm also planning a floating glyph texture with a cyan ring, inner hexagram, and dots on a transparent background. For the layout, I'm working out depth constants so book rows sit correctly in front of the camera plane without clipping, and I'm building helper arrays for book colors and textures to cycle through, along with randomized row generation for book sizes and placement.

Still working out compartment layouts...

Still working out scroll pyramid positions, then laying out the book row, an orb on its stand sized to clear the shelf above, and a small candle with a flat book stack on the right side.

For the second compartment, I'm placing a scroll jar on the left, another book row, an hourglass in the center, and two potions nearby, all checked against the shelf height clearance.

Moving to compartment 3, I'm stacking flat tomes topped with a candle on the left, verifying the flame stays under the height limit, then laying out another book row in the middle followed by a small cyan orb and a crystal with scrolls on the right.

For the top shelf, I'm placing an open book on the left, a larger central orb with a stand, an owl figure, and candles resting on small book stacks, then adding a crescent moon and scattered stars behind the center to fill out the composition.

Now I'm working out the crest shape above the shelf, calculating a gothic pointed arch outline using trigonometric curves to taper from a wide base up to a peaked apex.

I'm giving the moon and stars a flat pale gold glow instead of gilt paint since gilt can't actually glow, then adding a gilt torus ring behind the moon as an emblem, and sketching a gilt strip to follow the arch outline as a border.

Still writing sweep code...

Defining geometry helpers...

I'm double-checking my rotation math applies lean then yaw correctly, confirming the Euler order matches standard conventions, then moving on to defining each piece like the spine box using the computed position and rotation.

Still placing book pieces...

Still working out the box dimensions...

Pages should sit recessed slightly from the cover edges so they look tucked in rather than flush. Now I'm sketching spine decal designs for the texture variety, starting with horizontal gold band patterns for the first style.

Writing the row generator function...

Writing scroll and orb geometry...

Simplifying the claws to plain vertical cone shapes instead of tilted ones, then adding a glowing sphere for the gem itself, sized and textured to match its color. I'm working out the geometry so the torus ring sits snugly against the sphere's lower curve, matching radii so everything lines up visually with the stem beneath it.

Now I'm moving on to the remaining decorative pieces -- hourglass, potion bottle, crystal, candle, and wall sconces. For the crystal shape, I'm building it from a cluster of tilted octahedrons of varying heights and rotations to give it a faceted, jagged look.

I'm also budgeting part counts to stay under the triangle/object limit -- books alone account for roughly 225 parts, so everything else needs to stay lean. For the wall panels and shelf boards, I'm applying a wood grain texture function with adjustable axis orientation so the grain runs correctly along each surface.

Now I'm writing the paint function for the back wall star pattern, using a cellular noise function to create star-like cells blended against a dark purple base color, with brighter cells picked out in a warm gold tone. Writing frieze SVG loop...

Now I'm sketching the spiral SVG with an expanding radius path and a circle backdrop, plus a rune-textured page background with rows of small randomized glyph strokes.

Drafting the glyph texture with concentric circles, a hexagram, and tick marks around the edge, then moving on to the orb gradient texture generator.

Writing SVG gradient code...

Now I'm positioning the candle flame geometry, placing an outer orange ellipse above the wick with a glow effect, then an inner ellipse for the flame core.

Still writing SVG code...
